newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open near unchanged on Christmas Eve.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open near unchanged on Christmas Eve.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices began a quiet trading session little changed on Tuesday.
Trading will end early on Christmas Eve. The U.S. Treasury market will close at 1400 EST/1900 GMT, three hours earlier than usual.
A quiet session is expected with many market participants already on vacation and others planning to go home at midday.
Nonetheless, the market will get two reports that acquire enhanced significance at this time of year -- the BTM/Schroders and the Redbook weekly store sales reports.
The BTM/Schroders store sales report for the week ended December 21 is due at 0900 EST/1400 GMT. A forecast is not available but in the prior week, the report recorded a 0.7 percent sales gain.

The report due at 0900 EST/1400 GMT encompasses the last weekend of the Christmas holiday shopping season, a period usually viewed as a test of consumers' ability to spend. Since consumer spending fuels about 70 percent of the nation's economic growth, the financial markets watch that spending trend closely in an attempt to determine how strongly the economy can grow in the months ahead.
The BTM/Schroders store sales report is rumored to show a sales gain topping one percent but that rumor did not appear to be hurting the market.
The Lynch, Jones & Ryan Redbook store sales report is due at 1455 EST/1955 GMT, after the market is closed.
In the week ended December 14, the Redbook report recorded a 0.6 percent store sales gain.
In early trade, the 6-1/2-percent 30-year benchmark Treasury bond edged up 1/32 to 98-29/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
The two-year note rose was unchanged at 99-26/32, yielding 5.85 percent.

"We got the early read on Mitsubishi (store sales report) and it certainly was not indicative of weakness, but you're not seeing much reaction," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and money market analyst at Dean Witter Reynolds.
Flanagan said trading volume will be on the thin side.
"You saw that starting yesterday and you'll see that for the rest of the week," he said.
The five-year note was unchanged at 99-31/32 to yield 6.13 percent. The ten-year note was unchanged at 101-4/32, yielding 6.34 percent.
The three-month Treasury bill rate was unchanged at 4.95 percent. The six-month bill rate was off one basis point to 5.07 percent. The year bill rate was down one basis point to 5.21 percent.
